Grammy.com's "Inside Elephant 6" feature, describing the collective rather than this band alone: it "has inspired acts like Arcade Fire, the Shins, and Tame Impala."

Mark Kemp/Rolling Stone via uDiscover: "before he was a midnight vulture, Beck was a subversive folkie inspired equally by Sonic Youth and Mississippi John Hurt." AllMusic prose: Stereopathetic Soulmanure "hewed closer to the aural assault of art-minded bands like Sonic Youth." A biography: during his teens Beck discovered Sonic Youth, Pussy Galore and X.
A biography: from the late 1990s he merged his junkyard style with psychedelic rock, electronic music, tropicalia, and the music of Nick Drake and Serge Gainsbourg.
PopMatters: Siouxsie and the Banshees, the Slits and X-Ray Spex "all boasted singers that introduced new tones and techniques" and had "an even greater influence on later Riot Grrrl successors."

Multiple pieces on London's Elliott School describe Joe Goddard and Alexis Taylor meeting schoolmate Kieran Hebden (Four Tet) there in the early '90s and finding a mentor in him; the primary source article (Public Pressure magazine) could not be directly re-fetched.

Dan Ozzi, Noisey/Vice (Jan 20, 2014): described as "the Fugazi for the internet age of punk"; independently corroborated with the same framing by David Anthony, The A.V. Club (Aug 20, 2015). A critic comparison rather than a first.
Documented Elephant 6 scene overlap rather than a stated influence -- no first-person source has been found for this one.
Apple Music's editorial "Pulp: Influences": inspirations run well beyond the Kinks, from ABBA's Swedish disco to the glam-rock strut of Bowie and T. Rex.
Pitchfork describes Magnolia Electric Co. as a direct, intentional continuation of Neil Young's mid-1970s Tonight's the Night/Zuma era.
Music Musings names Talk Talk as an influence on Spiritualized, a connection that recurs across critical writing on Talk Talk's Hex-era work.
Treble review of Emergency & I draws the Fugazi lineage; snippet-only source, page 403'd on direct re-fetch attempt, flagged weaker-tier.

The CU Independent: "His [Josh Conway's] musical influences, spanning R&B, jazz, and indie rock, as well as Tame Impala, Radiohead, D'Angelo, and The Strokes, are evident in the dense yet transparent textures he creates in the studio."
AllMusic's band biography names their influences as a diverse set including the Pogues, Joy Division, Bruce Springsteen, Bjork, U2 and New Order. No first-person corroboration found.

The Dowsers describes Hecker's early work as fusing "the dry, pulsating rhythms of techno with the bare minimalism of Brian Eno" (journalistic characterization, not a first-person quote); Hecker has also spoken (Spin, 2019) about deliberately positioning his music against Eno's own definition of ambient.

Wikipedia's citation of a 2018 Zoe Camp profile states Turnstile cite Bad Brains among their own influences; Grammy.com and Hypebeast separately frame Turnstile's Baltimore/DC scene lineage as descending directly from Bad Brains.
Grammy.com and Hypebeast both frame Turnstile's hardcore lineage as running through Minor Threat, in pieces specifically about the band rather than general genre history.
Hypebeast's hardcore-lineage piece places Turnstile downstream of Black Flag, though this framing is general hardcore history rather than a Turnstile-specific citation.

Pitchfork's review of George Clanton's Slide (Miles Bowe, 2018): "Like Ariel Pink before him, Clanton throws himself into his music without any self-conscious concern for cool -- and throws himself about in breathtakingly physical live shows that bring to mind a young John Maus."
The Irish Times' review of Prelude to Ecstasy described the band as having "borrowed from 1980s acts such as Kate Bush and Siouxsie and the Banshees."
Wikipedia, citing Stylus Magazine's review: "nobody's been able to pull this off so well since Joy Division."
Louder: White's path to the blues ran through study of the Gun Club, Captain Beefheart, Bob Dylan and Led Zeppelin.
A Sputnik Music / Last.fm bio, mirrored across both sites, naming Drive Like Jehu as an influence -- aggregator text with no named origin.
